title: The studio wakes
panels: A dark return monitor faces six empty folding chairs. One worklight clicks on.
At the back door a little keyboard tries a loose key in the lock. A chord comes out.
Tracking slides out of the tape drawer and politely closes it behind himself.
Clank squeezes between two chairs. His tower takes both seats with him.
Cue unrolls a neglected script, looks for an audience and finds the dark monitor.
Gruff’s giant cable hand emerges from a knot, gently straightening one bent chair.

title: First company
panels: Chip unfolds one wing from beneath a low shelf; dust shakes off the disk.
Tabby tries to brighten her face. One green ring flickers and the crooked ear dips.
Hertz fills with snow. Tracking nudges his aerial until the static clears.
Wide: the gang arranges the chairs toward the monitor. Gruff supplies the long lead.
The band builds a beat from case, keys, rim and cable. One empty socket remains.
Tabby thanks the empty seats; a turn of the lens makes them look like front-row boxes.

title: The close-up test
panels: From the lens, shelves become an opera balcony for two beats. Cut back to masking tape.
Gruff ties himself smaller to fit Clank’s close-up mark. One huge foot still sticks out.
Tabby mouths a note in her coat collar, then lifts her head and lets it out.
Clank finally raises a hand to speak. Everyone has turned; the return monitor is still dark.
The keyboard displays one lonely word. The others lean over to read it.
Watt stretches his plug towards the wall; it stops just short. He holds it there, hopeful.

title: Build the picture
panels: Chip’s crest peeks up from a sketch on the cutting table. A drawn wing and his real wing align.
Tracking threads an old reel. Hertz shows a single frame of a packed auditorium.
Cue turns his last page: blank. Tabby folds the paper into a little balcony.
The band plays as rehearsal scenery unfolds; the paper balcony casts an impossibly big shadow.
Amp’s blue guitar fills the foreground; Thrum throws the last chord back as an echo.
Click cuts the band off with both mallets. The echo answers from the imaginary gallery.

title: Stand by
panels: The return light blinks. Everyone scurries to their mark for the big broadcast.
Cue holds up STAND BY, then looks around his card to see if it worked.
Tabby sidesteps until she stands right beside the card. Her ear flops against Cue.
Clank hoists an old ON AIR box. Watt plugs it in. It glows in his hands.
Gruff inhales, cheeks and coat swelling. Chip has to shuffle sideways to avoid them.
Watt reads MAX LOAD on a plug, then opens both arms as if measuring the whole cast.

title: Be kind, rewind
panels: Watt hugs whoever fits; Gruff carefully adds one finger rather than crushing the pile.
Chip lifts a box marked BE KIND. The band quiets to listen to it. Nothing.
Tracking rewinds. In apparent reverse motion the gang un-hugs into its earlier positions.
Their synchronized reverse steps turn into a strut. Cable shadows widen into triumphal arches.
In their heads Gruff plucks a cathedral-sized bass; cut to his tiny tub rattling across tape.
The amplifier plays a stadium chord; match back to his little blue guitar and its loose jack.

title: Zero
panels: The imagined gallery rises as one. Smash cut to the real six empty chairs.
Hertz counts down on glass. Each numeral lights Tabby’s face a little less.
Zero. The monitor is black. Clank has his mouth open, waiting for applause.
Close: Tabby hears the little hum of the room. She sings to the people beside her.
Chip gives ten with two wings and immediately loses count. Cue mouths Places.
The answering voices come from all around Tabby. For the first time she looks at her friends, not the lens.

title: Home
panels: The crew lift the return monitor onto a crate. Gruff plugs his lead into the correct return.
The fantasy theatre opens wide on the harmony. Same patched clothes, same blue guitar, enormous light.
Back on the boards, the monitor shows THEIR band with a tiny delay. They wave; the picture waves back.
Home. The gang bunches round the screen and the company camera snaps a portrait.
Hold the photograph against the imaginary gold proscenium a moment longer.
Back in the tiny room, one soft ear flops after the shutter. Cut on the release.
